call.text: Moshi’s theoretical latency of 160 ms is achieved by the model’s streaming, hierarchical architecture that is pretrained with an acoustic delay of 2 and finetuned with an acoustic delay of 1, which together set the target delay for real‑time operation【MOSHI:5.3:c083】. This design choice is highlighted in the introduction as giving Moshi a theoretical latency of 160 ms, which is lower than the 230 ms average measured in natural conversations across ten languages【MOSHI:1:c005】. In practice, Moshi runs with a latency of about 200 ms, as reported in the abstract【MOSHI:abstract:c002】. This practical latency is still below the typical natural‑conversation response time of a few hundred milliseconds and specifically lower than the 230 ms average observed in real human dialogue【MOSHI:1:c005】.
